items.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: And Buddy Collette paid me a wonderful compliment once. My dad gave him his first job. And he told me when I was playing one time

ctx.x: And that’s good advice about knowing the lyrics to a song.

Right. And Buddy Collette paid me a wonderful compliment once. My dad gave him his first job. And he told me when I was playing one time, he says, “You know what? You play a melody just like Frank Sinatra sings.” And I said, “Oh really?” And he said, “You’re singing all the time.” And I said yeah, well my aunt made us learn, if you’re going to play [sings] In my solitude you haunt me. We had to learn that. We had to learn. And I said I don’t know it, I just want to play it, and she’d say, “No, learn all those…
like an extension of the human voice. I’ve heard that said. I don’t know if it’s true why a trumpet wouldn’t be, but I have done that.
